notes.title: Firm foundation (He Won't) by Cody Carnes
Sermon Notes
notes.content:
When you have an encounter with Christ you need to culture a life around God.

@t@50:40 

To be holy set apart to be holy for God.

We are in the world we do not belong to the world. We are in the world but we are not of the world.

There are two ways of understanding holiness, two ways to be set apart.
	Holiness is something that happens from the "outside-in."
	Jesus offers a different understanding of Holiness 
			Holiness is from from the "inside-out."

From Holiness 1 You can live according to the "list of following Christ" and still be far from God. You can do all the right things with all the wrong spirit. This leads to having the love of God contingent on what you do. 

From Holiness 2 True transformation comes from within not from the external. 

$ The goal of Holiness is that it goes into our heart and spills into our hands, but if you only focus on the outside we will find ourselves missing the kind of Holiness Jesus wants for us. 

You need to build your identity around God to move towards an inside out Holiness. 

You can't have the foundation of your faith on an experience of God. You will miss out on the living God. @1:00:55 He says it better 

$ The essence of Holiness is about love.

Holiness is not ultimately an achievement, but a gift of God's grace.

@1:08:46 If you seek holiness you will not find it. If you seek Jesus you will find holiness.

@t@1:09:50  When you dwell in the presence of God the presence of God becomes strong.

notes.title: Mark 7:2-5 & Mark 7:14-15
notes.content:
Mark 7:2-5 And Pharisees and some of the teachers of the law who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus and saw some of his disciples eating food with hands that were defiled, that is, unwashed. The Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they give their hands ceremonial washing, holding to the tradition of the elders. When they come from the marketplace they do not eat unless they wash. And they observe many other traditions, such as the washing of cups, pitchers and kettles. So the Pharisees and teachers of the law asked Jesus, "Why don't your disciples live according to the tradition of the elders instead of eating their defiled hands?" 

^^@51:20^^Mark 7:14-15 Jesus called the crows to him and said, "Listen to me, everyone, and understand this. Nothing outside a person can defile them by going into them. Rather, it is what comes out of a person that defiles them."

notes.title: 1 Corinthians 1:2
notes.content: To you who have been called by God to be his own holy people. He made you holy by means of Christ Jesus.

notes.title: Analogy of how to make tea to Christ
notes.content:
There are two ways of making tea 
	dipping the tea bag in and pulling it out and repeating that
	just letting the tea bag soak in the water
we can compare this to our spiritual life, we can either be a dipper and dip in and out of Christianity or we can soak in the glory of God
